docs.title: Reports
docs.text: Reports are generated from each Xania checkout the site is built from. See Xania versions. Each version has an overview, assessments with interactive charts, an area catalogue and CSV downloads. When there's more than one version, a Compare page shows how they differ.

docs.title: Running it yourself
docs.text:
python -m pip install -e .[site]
python -m xania_explorer serve                       # ../xania, live preview at http://127.0.0.1:8000
python -m xania_explorer serve --target upstream=../xania-upstream --target fork=../xania

serve rebuilds whenever an area file changes. When the C++ loader changes, update the parser in xania_explorer/areafile/ and the area file format guide together. Each parser function cites the C++ function it ports.

docs.title: Architecture and game loop
docs.text: How the Xania server is put together and how time passes in the game. Paths are relative to xania/src/.

docs.title: Two processes
docs.text:
Process Source Job doorman doorman/ Owns the telnet port (MUD_PORT, default 9000). Handles telnet negotiation (TelnetProtocol.cpp), DNS and connection channels. Survives xania restarts, so players stay connected across a reboot. xania everything else The game. Talks to doorman over a Unix socket (/tmp/.xania-{port}-{user}) using fixed packets (doorman_protocol.h): INIT, CONNECT, DISCONNECT(_ACK), RECONNECT, MESSAGE, INFO (ip, port, ansi, hostname), ECHO_ON/OFF, AUTHORIZED, GO_AHEAD.

The apps/ directory has offline tools that link the game code: areas (a DOT graph of how areas connect), map (a DOT map of rooms) and pfu (a player-file upgrader). Both DOT tools print part of their output to stdout instead of the output file.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Read from environment variables (Configuration.cpp). The defaults are in mud-settings-dev.sh.

Variable Used for MUD_AREA_DIR area.lst, the .are and .prg files, tipfile.txt MUD_DATA_DIR player/ (player files), gods/, system/ (ban.lst, notes.txt, bugs.txt, typos.txt, ideas.txt) MUD_HTML_DIR static and generated web pages MUD_PORT doorman listen port

docs.title: Boot
docs.text:
main.cpp runs these steps in order:

  1. init_socket
  2. boot_db (db.cpp:190):
  3. assign gsn_* skill numbers;
  4. load every area file in area.lst order (see the area format spec);
  5. resolve exits (map_exit_destinations);
  6. sort the areas;
  7. reset every area once (area_update; each area starts at maximum age);
  8. set up wiznet.
  9. MudImpl::boot: load tips, bans and notes.
  10. game_loop.

docs.title: The game loop
docs.text:
MudImpl.cpp:180. Each iteration is one pulse, and the loop sleeps until the next quarter-second (PULSE_PER_SECOND = 4, Constants.hpp). Each pulse:

  1. Read input from doorman.
  2. For each connection: decrement the character's wait (lag). If the wait is zero, run one queued command: pager, interpret (InterpreterImpl.cpp), or nanny for login and character creation.
  3. update_handler (update.cpp:856), described below.
  4. Flush output. If output fails, a character above level 1 is saved and disconnected.

One command per pulse. Skills add lag through wait (in pulses; each skill's beats value in the skill table). That lag is the main limit on how fast actions can happen.

docs.title: Update timers
docs.text:
Timer Period Function What it does area random 30–90 s (PULSE_AREA = 60 s, ±50%) area_update → Area::update Ages each area and resets it when it's old enough (see world model) mobile 4 s mobile_update (update.cpp:242) Special functions, mobprog random triggers, scavenging, wandering violence 3 s violence_update (fight.cpp:102) One combat round for everyone who's fighting (multi_hit) tick ("point") 30 s char_update, obj_update, weather_update, count_update, tips HP/mana/move regen (hit_gain etc.), hunger and thirst, affects wearing off, idle players moved to limbo, object decay, game time and weather every pulse 0.25 s aggr_update (update.cpp:196) Aggressive mobs attack visible players every pulse 0.25 s collect_all_garbage Frees extracted characters and objects

A combat round (3 s) is therefore 12 pulses, and a tick (30 s) is 10 rounds.

docs.title: Level bands
docs.text:
Constants.hpp: MAX_LEVEL = 100, hero = 91. Levels 92 and up are immortal ranks (Avatar 92, Angel 93, Demi 94, Immortal 95, God 96, Deity 97, Supreme 98, Creator 99, Implementor 100).

Mobs can be above 100: Dell's priest is level 112.

docs.title: Area file format (.are)
docs.text:
This is the reference spec for Xania's area files, written from the C++ loader. Line references point into xania/src/ (e.g. db.cpp:395). The Python port in xania_explorer/areafile/ follows the same structure, so each section here corresponds to one parser function.

Severity. The C++ treats some problems as fatal (exit(1), so the MUD won't boot). Others it only logs (logger.bug) and then carries on with a default. Each rule below says which.

docs.title: 1. Loading model
docs.text:
• area/area.lst lists the files to load, one word each, ending at a word starting with $. Files are loaded in that order (db.cpp:225). A name of - means stdin, which nothing uses. .are files that aren't listed are never loaded. Five are currently unlisted: CausewayToImmortality, HelpLore, LairOfTheShadowCouncil, TantricObstacles and proto. Three of them (HelpLore, LairOfTheShadowCouncil, proto) would be fatal to load, and Causeway has invalid attack types; see the area catalogue (see Xania versions).
  • version.are is generated from version.are.in at build time (in the repo it's an empty file).
  • A file is a sequence of sections: #NAME, then the section body. #$ ends the file (db.cpp:241). Section names are matched case-insensitively. An unknown name, or any non-# character where a section should start, is fatal.
  • Mobs, objects, rooms, resets, shops, specials and mobprogs belong to the most recently loaded #AREA. That can be an #AREA from a previous file if this file has none. Help-only files (Help.are, HelpGroups.are, …) and Socials.are have no #AREA header.
  • Vnums (virtual numbers) are global across all files. A duplicate mob, object or room vnum is fatal. Vnums are stored as sh_int (16-bit signed).
  • Cross-file references (exit destinations, reset targets) are resolved after every file is loaded (db.cpp:280).

docs.title: 2. Primitive tokens
docs.text:
Every field is read by one of these functions (db.cpp:1241-1470). Leading whitespace is always skipped.

Token Reader Grammar Notes number fread_number :1267 [+-]digits then optionally \|number a\|b means a + b. Consumes one trailing space; any other character is pushed back, so 1d6+2 reads as 1 then d. A non-digit is fatal. flag fread_flag :1356 letters and/or digits, then optionally \|flag Each letter sets one bit: A–Z are bits 0–25 and a–z are bits 26–51. A run of the same letter counts once (AAB = AB). 0 means no flags. Digits are added as a decimal value. string fread_string :1389 text up to ~ Multi-line. ~ can't appear inside. EOF ends the string silently. string-eol fread_string_eol :1406 rest of the line Used only by #SOCIALS. word try_fread_word :1438 non-space run, or '...' / "..." Fatal at EOF, including a final word with no whitespace after it. letter fread_letter :1254 one non-space char Used for record markers (#, D, E, A, S, …). spnumber try_fread_spnumber :1310 a spell slot number, or spell name~ Quoted spell names are fatal. An unknown spell name is fatal. dice Dice::from_file (Dice.cpp:6) NdS+B A wrong separator, N<=0 or S<=0 is only logged. to-eol fread_to_eol :1422 discard to end of line Text after a reset's arguments is a free-form comment.

Prefix-matched words. Enum-valued words are matched by case-insensitive prefix, first match in table order (matches_start, string_utils.cpp:258). For example, stand gives Standing, s as a body size gives small, and s as an attack gives slice.

Flag letters in headers vs files. C++ headers write bits 26 and up as doubled letters (aa, bb, …; StandardBits.hpp). In an area file you write the single lower-case letter: a = bit 26 = aa.

docs.title: 3. #AREA — header
docs.text:
Area.cpp:14

#AREA
<filename>~                 ignored
<short name>~               shown by 'areas' and used in logs
<description>~              "{min max} Author  Long Name", or "{ ALL } ..." / "{None} ..."
<lowest vnum> <highest vnum>
  • Level band = sscanf("{%d %d}") on the description. If it doesn't match, the area is "all levels".
  • Vnum range. The declared range is then extended by every mob and object vnum in the file (Area::define_vnum, Area.cpp:45), but not by room vnums. Quirk: if either declared bound is 0, the first mob/object vnum replaces both.
  • The effective range matters because Area::reset() resets rooms by iterating lowest..highest vnum (Area.cpp:81). A room outside its area's range never has its resets run by that area.

docs.title: 4. #MOBILES — mob prototypes
docs.text:
MobIndexData.cpp:28. The records repeat until #0.

#<vnum>
<keywords>~
<short descr>~              "a priest of Wandera"  (leading articles lower-cased on load)
<long descr>~               room line when standing at default position
<look description>~
<race>~                     race_table name, prefix match (handler.cpp:61); unknown → "unique", silently
<act flags> <affected_by flags> <alignment> <group>
<level> <hitroll> <hit dice> <mana dice> <damage dice> <attack word>
<ac pierce> <ac bash> <ac slash> <ac exotic>
<offensive flags> <immune flags> <resist flags> <vuln flags>
<start pos> <default pos> <sex> <gold>
<form flags> <body-part flags> <size> <material>
Field Type Values / notes act flag CharActFlag.hpp: B Sentinel, C Scavenger, F Aggressive, G StayArea, H Wimpy, J Train, K Practice, L Sentient, M Talkative, O Undead, Q Cleric, R Mage, S Thief, T Warrior, U NoAlign, V NoPurge, a Healer, b Gain, c UpdateAlways, d CanBeRidden. A (Npc) is always set on load. The class bits (Q/R/S/T) pick the NPC's to-hit curve in HitChance.cpp. affected_by flag AffectFlag.hpp (Sanctuary H, Haste V, Flying T, …) alignment number −1000..1000 by convention group number NPC group id (used for assisting) level number not capped at load; Dell's priest is level 112 hitroll number added to the to-hit roll hit / mana / damage dice Rolled per instance. Damage dice are used only when the mob is unarmed (fight.cpp:465). attack word, prefix Attacks.cpp table; sets the damage type. Unknown → logged, uses hit. ac ×4 number order is ArmourClass.hpp: pierce, bash, slash, exotic. More negative is better. offensive flag OffensiveFlag.hpp: A AreaAttack, B Backstab, C Bash, D Berserk, E Disarm, F Dodge, H Fast, I Kick, J KickDirt, K Parry, L Rescue, N Trip, P–U Assist*, V Headbutt, W Slow imm / res / vuln flag ToleranceFlag.hpp start / default pos word, prefix Dead Mortal Incap Stunned Sleeping Resting Sitting Fighting Standing. Unknown → logged, default. sex word, prefix neutral / male / female (checked in that order). Unknown is fatal. gold number form / parts flag MorphologyFlag.hpp, BodyPartFlag.hpp size word, prefix tiny small medium large huge giant. Unknown → logged, medium. material word Materials.cpp; unknown → default material

On load, race flags are ORed in. act, affected_by, off, imm, res, vuln, form and parts all get the race's values from Races.cpp added. The catalogue shows file values only, so for example an elf mob also resists Charm even if the file doesn't say so.

docs.title: 5. #OBJECTS — object prototypes
docs.text:
db.cpp:574-776. The records repeat until #0.

#<vnum>
<keywords>~
<short descr>~
<room description>~         empty → logged
<material>~                 note: a ~string, unlike mobs
<type word> <extra flags> <wear flags>
[,<wear string>~]           optional custom wear message (Death's "Wear Strings")
<v0> <v1> <v2> <v3> <v4>    grammar depends on type, see below
<level> <weight> <cost> <condition letter>
{ A <location> <modifier> | E <keywords>~ <description>~ }*
  • type: prefix match in ObjectType.hpp enum order (light, scroll, wand, staff, weapon, treasure, armor, potion, clothing, furniture, trash, container, drink, key, food, money, boat, npccorpse, pccorpse, fountain, pill, map, bomb, portal), or the type number. Unknown → logged, light.
  • extra flags ObjectExtraFlag.hpp: A Glow, B Hum, C Dark, D Lock, E Evil, F Invis, G Magic, H NoDrop, I Bless, J/K/L Anti-Good/Evil/Neutral, M NoRemove, N Inventory, O NoPurge, P RotDeath, Q VisDeath, R ProtectContainer, S NoLocate, T SummonCorpse, U Unique. NoRemove on a non-weapon is fatal.
  • wear flags ObjectWearFlag.hpp: A Take, B Finger, C Neck, D Body, E Head, F Legs, G Feet, H Hands, I Arms, J Shield, K About, L Waist, M Wrist, N Wield, O Hold, P TwoHands, Q Ears.
  • condition: P 100, G 90, A 75, W 50, D 25, B 10, R 0; anything else 100.
  • A affects: location modifier. Locations are from AffectLocation.hpp: 1 Str, 2 Dex, 3 Int, 4 Wis, 5 Con, 12 Mana, 13 Hit, 14 Move, 17 Ac, 18 Hitroll, 19 Damroll, 20–24 saves, …
  • Validators: ScrollTargetValidator rejects scrolls whose spells have incompatible targets (fatal; ScrollTargetValidator.cpp). It isn't ported yet.

docs.title: Value grammar by type
docs.text:
Type v0 v1 v2 v3 v4 weapon weapon-type word (exotic sword dagger spear mace axe flail whip polearm; prefix) dice number dice sides attack word (prefix) weapon flags: A Flaming, B Frost, C Vampiric, D Sharp, E Vorpal, F TwoHands, G Poisoned, I Plagued, J Lightning, K Acid container capacity (number) container flags key vnum number number drink, fountain capacity current liquid word number (poisoned) number wand, staff spell level max charges charges spnumber number potion, pill, scroll, bomb spell level spnumber spnumber spnumber spnumber everything else (armor, light, food, …) flag flag flag flag flag

For armor, v0–v3 are the AC bonuses (pierce/bash/slash/exotic). They're read as flags, so plain numbers work. After reading, spell slot numbers are translated to skill numbers (db.cpp:746); bombs also translate v4. Slot numbers are listed in SkillTables.cpp and must never change.

Weapon damage is dice(v1, v2) × weapon skill %. The average is v1 × (v2 + 1) / 2. The balance rule in entity_balance.cpp allows an average of level/2 + 4 (a little more for two-handers).

docs.title: 6. #ROOMS
docs.text:
db.cpp:395. The records repeat until #0.

#<vnum>
<name>~
<description>~
<room flags> <sector number>
{ D<dir> <exit description>~ <exit keywords>~ <locks> <key vnum> <to vnum>
| E <keywords>~ <description>~ }*
S

(Unlike stock ROM, there's no area-number field before the flags.)

  • room flags RoomFlag.hpp: A Dark, C NoMob, D Indoors, J Private, K Safe, L Solitary, M PetShop, N NoRecall, O ImpOnly, P GodsOnly, Q HeroesOnly, R NewbiesOnly, S Law. Hack: rooms 3000–3399 always get Law (db.cpp:418). Rooms with no exit leading anywhere get NoMob after load (db.cpp:801).
  • sector SectorType.hpp: 0 Inside, 1 City, 2 Field, 3 Forest, 4 Hills, 5 Mountain, 6 SwimmableWater, 7 NonSwimmableWater, 8 Unused, 9 Air, 10 Desert. Invalid → logged, Inside.
  • dir: 0 N, 1 E, 2 S, 3 W, 4 Up, 5 Down. Out of range is fatal. A later D for the same direction replaces the earlier one.
  • locks: 0 no door, 1 door, 2 door + pick-proof, 3 door + pass-proof, 4 door + both.
  • to vnum: a room vnum. -1 is a cosmetic exit that leads nowhere. Below −1 is one-way to abs(vnum). 0, or a room that doesn't exist, leaves the exit unresolved (it leads nowhere).
  • Exit consistency (db.cpp:804): for a two-way exit A→B, if B's reverse exit leads somewhere other than A, the loader logs Fix_exits. If B's reverse exit leads nowhere, the C++ dereferences a null pointer. Mark deliberately asymmetric exits one-way (negative vnum).

docs.title: 7. #RESETS — repopulation script
docs.text:
Parsed by db.cpp:301 and run by reset_room (db.cpp:829). Each line is <cmd> <if_flag> <args…> [comment] until S. * starts a comment line. if_flag is read and ignored. Text after the last argument is ignored, so it's used for comments (e.g. M 0 3011 1 3001 1 Concordius). An unknown command is fatal.

Resets are stored on rooms, not the area. The room each reset attaches to depends on the lines before it:

Cmd Args Attached to Behaviour at reset time M mob vnum, world max, room vnum, room max room arg3 (becomes "last room") Spawn the mob unless the world already has ≥ arg2 of it, or the room has ≥ arg4. If the room at vnum − 1 is a PetShop, the mob gets Pet. Sets "last mob". O obj vnum, (unused), room vnum room arg3 (becomes "last obj room") Skipped if any player is in the area or the room already has one. The object's cost is set to 0 (db.cpp:908), so floor loot can't be sold. P obj vnum, world limit, container obj vnum, count the last O's room (or the last M's room after G/E) Put up to arg4 copies into the first existing instance of the container. Skipped if the area is occupied. Limit: arg2 > 20 → 6, −1 → unlimited (999). Even past the limit there's a 1-in-5 chance to spawn anyway. G obj vnum, drop % the last M's room Give the item to the last spawned mob. A shopkeeper always gets it, as shop inventory. Otherwise it spawns with probability arg2%. arg2 outside 1..100 on a non-shopkeeper calls exit(1) at reset time, crashing a running MUD. E obj vnum, drop %, wear location the last M's room As G, then equips it at a Worn.hpp slot: 0 Light, 1/2 Finger L/R, 3/4 Neck, 5 Body, 6 Head, 7 Legs, 8 Feet, 9 Hands, 10 Arms, 11 Shield, 12 About, 13 Waist, 14/15 Wrist L/R, 16 Wield, 17 Hold, 18 Ears. D room vnum, direction, state (not stored) Applied once at load: 0 open, 1 closed, 2 closed + locked. The exit must be a door (fatal otherwise). Every reset restores each exit's saved door state. R room vnum, number of exits room arg1 Shuffles exits 0..arg2−1 (a maze). arg2 outside 0..6 is fatal.

G/E lines only take effect if the last M actually spawned. Spawn order matters: an area resets rooms in ascending vnum order, and each room runs its resets in file order.

docs.title: 8. #SHOPS
docs.text:
db.cpp:491. One line per shop, ending with a line containing just 0:

<keeper mob vnum> <buy type ×5> <profit buy %> <profit sell %> <open hour> <close hour> [comment]

The buy types are object type numbers (0 = slot unused; see the ObjectType table above). If the keeper mob doesn't exist, the C++ dereferences a null pointer.

docs.title: 9. #SPECIALS
docs.text: db.cpp:520. Lines are M <mob vnum> <spec_fun name> [comment], and * lines are comments, until S. The spec function name must exist in special.cpp (spec_lookup), otherwise it's fatal.

docs.title: 10. #MOBPROGS
docs.text:
MProgLoader.cpp:104. Lines are M <mob vnum> <file.prg> [comment], and * lines are comments, until S. The .prg file is read from the area dir. An unknown mob vnum, a missing file or an invalid file is fatal.

A .prg file (MProgLoader.cpp:76) has one or more blocks, then |:

>greet_prog 30~
if ispc($n)
    beg $n
endif
~
|

The triggers are: act, speech, rand, fight, hitprcnt, death, entry, greet, all_greet, give, bribe (all _prog). in_file_prog is rejected. The argument string's meaning depends on the trigger, usually a % chance or an amount. The interpreter is MProgImpl.cpp.

docs.title: 11. #HELPS
docs.text: Help.cpp:13. Each entry is <min level> <keywords>~ <text>~, ending at the keyword $ (conventionally 0 $~). A leading . in the text is stripped, which lets the text start with whitespace. Level −1 entries (e.g. DIKU) are visible to everyone.

docs.title: 12. #SOCIALS
docs.text: Socials.cpp:17. Each social is <name> followed by 8 lines (char-no-arg, others-no-arg, char-found, others-found, victim-found, char-not-found (unused), char-auto, others-auto), then a line containing #. $ on a line means an empty phrase. The section ends at #0. A missing # terminator stops social loading (logged).

docs.title: 14. Quick checklist for builders
docs.text:
• Put every new file in area.lst.
  • Keep mobs, objects and rooms inside the declared vnum range; rooms outside it won't reset.
  • G/E drop rate must be 1–100.
  • Mark one-way exits with a negative vnum.
  • Use spell name~, never 'spell name'.
  • Don't put NoRemove on anything but weapons.
  • Run python -m xania_explorer check before committing.

docs.title: World model
docs.text: How the world is put together at runtime. The file syntax is in the area format spec, and the per-area numbers are in the generated area catalogue (see Xania versions).

docs.title: Prototypes and instances
docs.text:
Area files define prototypes: MobIndexData and ObjectIndex, keyed by vnum. Resets create instances (Char via create_mobile, and Object) from those prototypes. When an instance is created:

  • Mobs (db.cpp:1034) roll HP from the hit dice, get race flags merged in, and get NPCs' stat adjustments by size (BodySize.cpp: bigger than medium gets bonus str/con).
  • Objects copy their prototype values. Objects created by an O reset (lying on the floor) get cost 0.
  • Each prototype keeps a live count of its instances. M and P resets use this to cap how many exist in the world.

docs.title: Areas
docs.text:
An area is a header plus a vnum range (Area.hpp). It owns its rooms only through that range: Area::reset() walks lowest..highest vnum and resets every room it finds there. The range is the declared one widened by the area's mob and object vnums, but not its room vnums.

area.lst currently loads 72 areas plus 6 header-less help/social/version files.

docs.title: Rooms and exits
docs.text:
• There are six directions: north, east, south, west, up, down. Each room has at most one exit per direction.
  • An exit has a destination, a door state (locks in the file, turned into IsDoor/PickProof/PassProof flags), a key vnum, keywords and a description.
  • Door state is stored twice. rs_flags is the reset state, set from the file's locks code plus any D resets. exit_info is the live state. Every room reset copies rs_flags into exit_info, for both sides of the door.
  • One-way exits have a negative destination in the file. Cosmetic exits (-1) lead nowhere.
  • Two-way exits are expected to be symmetric. The loader logs a Fix_exits bug otherwise (db.cpp:804).
  • Rooms with no exit leading anywhere get NoMob.
  • Rooms 3000–3399 (Midgaard) always get Law.
  • Important vnums (VnumRooms.hpp): Limbo 2, Chat 1200, Midgaard temple 3001 (where you recall to), altar 3054, Mud School entrance 3700.

docs.title: Resets
docs.text:
The area clock (Area.cpp:74, db.cpp:821):

  • An area pulse fires every 30–90 s (random, re-rolled each time). Each pulse adds 1 to every area's age.
  • An area resets when age >= 15. If it was empty at its last reset and nobody has entered since, the threshold is age >= 10. After a reset, age is set to a random 0–3. So an area that stays empty resets every 7–10 area pulses (~3.5–15 min), and one that's had players in it every 12–15 (~6–22 min). An area is flagged "empty" at reset time if no players are in it. The flag clears (and age drops to 0) when a player enters, so stepping in and out doesn't speed up resets.
  • Mud School (the area containing room 3700) has its age set to 10 after each reset and is never flagged empty. By this reading it resets every ~5 area pulses (~2.5–7.5 min). The comment in Area.cpp claims 1–2 minutes, which doesn't match.
  • Booting resets every area once.

Within a reset, rooms are processed in vnum order. Each room runs its reset list in file order: M spawns a mob, and the G/E lines after it equip that mob. Key rules (full table in the spec (§7)):

  • M caps the mob at arg2 in the world and arg4 in the room.
  • O and P are skipped while any player is in the area. Floor loot and container contents only refresh in empty areas.
  • A G/E drop rate (arg2) is a percent chance for normal mobs. Shopkeepers always get the item, as stock.
  • Pet-shop rule: a mob reset in the room after a PetShop room becomes a pet.

docs.title: Shops, specials, mob programs
docs.text:
• Shops attach to the keeper's mob prototype. They have buy types (object type numbers), profit percentages for buying and selling, and opening hours in game time.
  • Specials attach a C++ behaviour function (spec_* in special.cpp) to a mob. It runs on the mobile timer (every 4 s).
  • Mob programs are scripted triggers from .prg files. Currently 12 files are used by 29 mobs (MProgImpl.cpp).

docs.title: Inspecting the world from Python
docs.text:
from xania_explorer.areafile.world import load_world
w = load_world()                      # ../xania/area by default
w.mobs[12100].hit.average             # 7601.0
w.area_named("Dell.are").linked_areas # {'Plains of the North'}
[p for p in w.problems]               # load-integrity problems

docs.title: Characters: races, classes, stats and levelling
docs.text: How a player character is built and how it grows from level 1 to 91. Paths are relative to xania/src/. The Characters assessment applies these rules to every race and class.

docs.title: Creation
docs.text:
1. Race and class. There are 10 PC races and 4 classes. The race sets starting stats (MudImpl.cpp:831), and the creation-point total starts at the race's cost.
  2. Skills. Every character gets rom basics plus its <class> basics group free. The player then takes the <class> default package (40 points) or customises, buying groups and skills at their per-class cost (skills.cpp, group_add). Points are capped at 200.
  3. XP per level is fixed at creation from the total points (see below). Spending more on skills makes every level dearer.
  4. Entering the game (MudImpl.cpp:984):
  5. +3 to the class prime stat, except for dragons;
  6. 20 HP, 100 mana, 100 move;
  7. 3 trains and 5 practices;
  8. if points are below 40, extra trains of (40 − points + 1) / 2.

docs.title: Classes
docs.text:
From Class.cpp:

Class Prime stat HP roll per level Mana factor To-hit AC at level 0 → 32 Free weapon skill mage int 6–8 10 −1 → −47 dagger cleric wis 7–10 8 −1 → −51 mace knight str 10–14 6 −1 → −61 sword barbarian con 13–17 3 −1 → −63 axe
  • To-hit AC is interpolated by level and drives the chance to hit (see the combat guide).
  • Skill adept is 75% for every class. That's the most practising can teach; using a skill can improve it further.

docs.title: Races
docs.text:
From pc_race_table in Races.cpp:147. Each race has: - a creation-point cost; - an XP multiplier for each class; - up to 5 bonus skills; - base and maximum stats; - a body size.

The table is listed on the Characters page. Bonus skills are cheaper to learn: difficulty −1 and available by level 30 at the latest (skills.cpp:566).

Race also merges NPC-style flags: elves resist charm and are vulnerable to iron, dwarves resist poison and disease, and so on (Races.cpp, race_table).

docs.title: XP per level
docs.text:
exp_per_level(points) (skills.cpp:259) works like this: - Below 40 points: 1000 × class multiplier. - From 40 points: start at 1000. The next 10 points add 500, the 10 after that add 500 more, and the step then doubles for every following pair of 10s. Partial tens add pro rata. - The result is multiplied by the race's class multiplier and capped at 65,500.

A character levels when exp ≥ exp_per_level × (level + 1) (update.cpp:586). Every level costs the same, and reaching 91 takes 90 × that.

Points XP per level (×1.00) 40 (human, default) 1,000 45 (elf, dwarf) 1,250 50 (eagle, orc) 1,500 55 (minotaur, half-elf) 1,750 60 (hobbit, wolf) 2,000 80 (dragon) 4,000

docs.title: Stats
docs.text:
Five stats, each from 3 to 25. Their effects come from the bonus tables in Stats.cpp:

Stat Effect str str_app: hitroll and damroll bonus (Char.cpp:439), carry weight (handler.cpp:156), heaviest weapon you can wield (handler.cpp:175) int int_app.learn: practice gain (act_info.cpp:1604) and learn-by-use chance; mana gain above 15 wis wis_app: practices per level; mana gain above 15 dex dex_app.defensive: added to AC while awake (Char.cpp:200); movement gain con con_app.hitp: HP bonus per level; movement gain; HP regeneration (update.cpp:336)

Limits: - Trainable maximum: the race maximum, +2 for the prime stat, capped at 25 (handler.cpp:117). - Effective maximum with spells and items: the race maximum +4, or +6 for the prime stat (Char.cpp:192).

docs.title: Levelling up
docs.text:
advance_level (update.cpp:480) runs once per level gained:

  • HP: (con_app.hitp + random(class min..max)) × 9 / 10, at least 1.
  • Mana: random(0 .. factor² × (max(0, wis−15) + 2·max(0, int−15))), then (that + 150) / 300 + factor / 2. So below 16 int and wis a mage gains a flat 5 mana and a barbarian 1.
  • Move: random(1 .. (con + dex) / 6) × 9 / 10, at least 6.
  • Practices: wis_app.practice.
  • Trains: +1. A train buys +1 to a stat (up to its trainable maximum), +10 HP or +10 mana (act_move.cpp:1020).

docs.title: Practising skills
docs.text: Practising at a guild (act_info.cpp:1561) costs a practice. It raises the skill by int_app.learn / difficulty, where difficulty is the class's rating for that skill, up to the 75% adept limit. Beyond that, skills improve only through use (Learning.cpp).

docs.title: Combat and experience
docs.text: How a melee round is resolved, and how kills turn into experience. Paths are relative to xania/src/. The Combat & XP assessment applies these formulas across levels 1–91.

docs.title: The round
docs.text:
Every 3 seconds (PULSE_VIOLENCE), violence_update (fight.cpp:102) calls multi_hit once for each fighter.

Player attacks per round (fight.cpp:239):

Attack When 1st always extra if hasted (and not lethargic) 2nd chance = second attack skill / 2 % 3rd chance = third attack skill / 4 %

Backstab is a single blow.

Mob attacks per round (mob_hit, fight.cpp:292): - 1st: always. Mobs with the Backstab flag can open with a backstab on an unhurt victim. - Extra: if the mob is hasted or Fast. - Area attack: a mob with AreaAttack also swings at everyone else fighting it. - 2nd: warrior or thief mobs only, at skill max(25, level/2). - 3rd: warriors only, at skill level − 30, and only if the 2nd landed. - One special move: chosen at random from its offensive flags (bash, berserk, disarm, kick, dirt kick, trip).

docs.title: Hitting
docs.text:
HitChance (HitChance.cpp):

  1. The attacker's to-hit AC = interpolate(level, AC₀, AC₃₂) × weapon skill % − hitroll:
  2. interpolate is linear and keeps going past level 32 (db.cpp:1676);
  3. AC₀ and AC₃₂ come from the class (Characters) or, for mobs, from the class flag: warrior −76, thief −70, cleric −66, mage −63, default thief.
  4. Penalties: the to-hit AC is ×0.8 if the attacker can't see. Backstab subtracts skill/3 (an improvement).
  5. The victim's AC: the armour value for the damage type (pierce, bash, slash or exotic), plus the dex bonus while awake. It's ×0.8 if the victim is sleeping or stunned, ×0.9 if resting or sitting.
  6. Chance = both values made positive (minimum 1), as a ratio of attack to defence, clamped to 10–95%. A d100 roll below it hits.

Defences. Each is checked against a hit before damage (fight.cpp:1061):

Defence Needs Chance parry the defender wields a weapon skill/3 + level difference dodge — skill/3 + dex difference + level difference shield block the defender wears a shield skill/3 + level difference

Each has a minimum of 5%. Whips can't be parried or blocked.

Mob defensive skill = 15 + level/2 for warriors and thieves, level/3 for others (Char.cpp:213).

docs.title: Damage
docs.text:
one_hit (fight.cpp:410) then damage (fight.cpp:586):

  1. Base damage depends on what the attacker is holding:
Attacker Base damage armed weapon dice × weapon skill % unarmed mob its damage dice. The dice bonus became its damroll (db.cpp:1062) unarmed player random(1 + 4·skill/100, 2·level/3 · skill/100)
  1. Weapon effects on that base:
  2. sharp: ×2 on 2% of hits;
  3. vorpal: ×1.3 when the dice roll exactly their average;
  4. no shield worn: ×1.05.
  5. Enhanced damage: roll d100; if it's ≤ skill, add damage × roll / 100.
  6. The victim's position: ×2 if asleep or stunned, ×1.5 if resting.
  7. Backstab: ×(2 + level/10), or level/8 for daggers.
  8. Damroll: add damroll × min(100, skill) / 100. Damage is at least 1 and capped at 1,000.
  9. Adjustments in damage:
  10. octarine fire: +level/8 %;
  11. sanctuary: ÷1.6;
  12. protection from evil or good: −25%;
  13. parry, dodge or block can cancel the hit outright;
  14. immune: 0, resistant: −⅓, vulnerable: +½;
  15. material vulnerability (e.g. iron against elves): +½.
  16. On-hit effects: poisoned and plagued weapons cast their spell on 25% of hits.

docs.title: Mob stats
docs.text: create_mobile (db.cpp:1034): - HP: rolled from the hit dice. - Stats: all min(25, 11 + level/4), adjusted for class and size (+3 str and +2 con for warriors, +3 dex for thieves, and so on). - AC from the area file. - Skills from their level (see above). Weapon skill is 40 + 5·level/2 armed and 40 + 2·level unarmed. - Gold: random(gold/2, 3·gold/2).

docs.title: Experience
docs.text:
group_gain and xp_compute (fight.cpp:1338):

  1. Base XP from the level gap (victim − killer):
Gap ≤ −10 −5 −2 0 +2 +4 above +4 XP 0 11 55 85 120 160 150 + 20 per level above 4

In a group, the highest member's level counts. 2. Alignment: the killer's alignment drifts toward the opposite of the victim's. XP is then ×0.75–1.25 depending on both alignments (neutrals get ×1.25 for strongly good or evil victims). 3. Low and high levels: - below level 6: ×10 / (level + 4); - levels 36–69: ÷(1 + level/300); - levels 70+: ÷(1 + level/250), which is −36% at 91. 4. The played-time clock: quarter-hours played per level, clamped to 2–6, ÷6. Full XP needs an average of 1.5 hours played per level; faster players get as little as a third. Below level 15 the floor is 8 − level, so levels 1–2 always get full credit. 5. Randomness and grouping: ±25% random, then × your share of the group's levels × 1.5 (so ×1.5 solo). 6. Levelling: gain_exp advances a level each time XP passes exp_per_level × (level + 1) (see Characters). Heroes (91) stop gaining.

docs.title: Skills and magic
docs.text: How characters acquire and improve skills and spells, and how casting works. Paths are relative to xania/src/. The Skills & spells assessment applies these rules across levels 1–91.

docs.title: The skill table
docs.text:
skill_table (SkillTables.cpp) lists every skill and spell. Each has: - level per class: the level at which that class can learn it; - rating per class: the cost in creation points or trains, and the difficulty used when practising and learning by use; - minimum mana and beats (lag after use, in quarter-second pulses); - a slot number: area files refer to spells by slot (scrolls, potions and so on), so slots must never change.

Special ratings: - 0: the class can never learn the skill. - −1 (cross-class): learnable from level 60 at difficulty 8. - −2 (assassin): learnable at 30 with the assassin group, otherwise 60, at difficulty 5.

A race's bonus skills are capped at level 30 and are one difficulty step easier (skills.cpp:566).

docs.title: Getting skills
docs.text: Groups (group_table) bundle skills. At creation a character takes rom basics, its class basics, and either its class default package or a custom set. You can only practise skills you already know (at least 1%). Anything else must be bought later with trains through gain (skills.cpp:195).

docs.title: Improving skills
docs.text:
• Practising at a guild (act_info.cpp:1561) costs a practice and adds int_app.learn / difficulty, up to the class's adept limit (75%).
  • Using a skill can improve it further, up to 100% (check_improve, Learning.cpp). The chance depends on int, difficulty and level. A failed use can teach you more (1–3 points) than a success (1). Each improvement gives 2 × difficulty XP.
  • Mobs don't learn. Their skills come from their level and flags (Char.cpp:213).

docs.title: Casting
docs.text:
do_cast (magic.cpp):

  1. Mana cost = max(min_mana, 100 / (2 + level − level learned)) (magic.cpp:582). New spells are expensive and get cheap as you out-level them.
  2. Lag: the caster waits the spell's beats (12 pulses = 3 s for most attack spells).
  3. Success: the cast fails if d100 exceeds your skill %. A failure costs half the mana.
  4. Saving throws: the victim saves with chance 50 + victim level − caster level − saving throw, clamped to 5–95% (saves_spell, magic.cpp:546).

Direct-damage spells mostly roll random(table[level] / 2, table[level] × 2) from a per-level table in magic.cpp (get_direct_dmg_and_level) and halve it on a save. Several spells share a table: - acid blast, demonfire and exorcise; - fireball and harm; - lightning bolt, chain lightning and cause critical; - burning hands and cause serious; - magic missile and cause light; - colour spray, dispel evil and dispel good.

The exceptions roll dice: call lightning dice(level/2, 8) and energy drain dice(1, level). Breath weapons scale with the caster's HP.

Spell damage goes through damage() like melee, so sanctuary, resistances and vulnerabilities apply. Parry, dodge and shield block don't.

docs.title: Items and economy
docs.text: How objects become equipment, what keeps them balanced, and how gold moves. Paths are relative to xania/src/. The Weapons, Equipment and Economy assessments apply these rules across levels 1–91.

docs.title: Wearing things
docs.text:
• Level: you can't wear or wield an object above your level (act_obj.cpp:137).
  • No class restrictions: any class can wear anything.
  • Alignment flags: items with AntiGood, AntiEvil or AntiNeutral "zap" a wearer of that alignment off when they next gain XP (fight.cpp, group_gain).
  • Wear slots (Worn.hpp): light, two fingers, two necks, body, head, legs, feet, hands, arms, shield, about, waist, two wrists, wield, hold and ears.
  • Weapons: two-handed weapons rule out a shield. Your strength limits the heaviest weapon you can wield (handler.cpp:175).
  • Armour class: armour objects subtract their four AC values (pierce, bash, slash, exotic) from your AC in any armour slot (apply_ac, handler.cpp:363). Ac affects on any item change it further. A character starts at AC 0, so gear and dex are all the protection there is.

docs.title: The item-points rule
docs.text:
report_object (entity_balance.cpp) is the builders' balance check, reported by the immortal command immworth:

Bonus Points +1 to a stat 1 +1 hitroll or damroll 1 (½ on weapons) +7 HP, mana or move 1 flaming, frost, vampiric, sharp or vorpal 1 each AC or saving throws meant to be 1 per −1, but never counted (bug below)
  • Allowance: an item may carry level/10 + 1 points.
  • Weapon damage: a weapon's average damage, (n·s + n) / 2, may not exceed level/2 + 4, plus 5% for two-handers.
  • The bug: in AFFECT_DATA::worth (AFFECT_DATA.cpp:86) the AC and saving-throw case reads if (modifier < 0) if (modifier > 0), which is never true. So these bonuses are free.

docs.title: Where items come from
docs.text: Resets place every object in the world (see the area format): - Shop stock: items given to a shopkeeper, always present. - Mob drops: items given to or worn by a mob, spawned with a drop chance from 1 to 100%. - Floor and container items: these refresh only when the area is empty, and floor items have cost 0, so they can't be sold.

docs.title: Gold in
docs.text:
• Mobs: each instance carries random(gold/2, 3·gold/2) of its prototype's gold (db.cpp:1034). Autogold loots it from the corpse.
  • Sacrifice: sacrificing a corpse gives max(1, 2 × level) gold. Other objects give that much capped at their cost (act_obj.cpp:1435).
  • Money objects on the floor or in containers.
  • Selling to a shop that trades the item's type pays cost × sell %. A shop that already stocks the item pays nothing (act_obj.cpp:481).

docs.title: Gold out
docs.text:
• Shops charge cost × buy %. Wands and staves scale with their remaining charges.
  • The healer charges flat prices whatever your level (healer.cpp): cure light 1,000, serious 1,600, critical 2,500, heal 5,000, blindness 2,000, disease 1,500, poison 2,500, remove curse 5,000, refresh 500, mana 1,000.
  • Pets from pet shops, and giving gold to other players.

docs.title: About the assessments
docs.text:
Each assessment covers one game system and answers one question: how balanced is it for a character levelling from 1 to 91 (hero)? The reports are generated for every Xania version the site is built from. Each has interactive charts and a CSV of the underlying data.

System Question Builds on Characters How do classes and races grow, and what does each cost in XP? — Weapons What weapons can each class find and wield at each level? — Equipment How much armour and hitroll/damroll can a character wear at each level? — Combat & XP What does a fight look like at each level, and how many kills does a level take? Characters, Weapons, Equipment, Mobs Skills & spells What can each class learn as it levels, and do attack spells keep up? Characters, Combat Economy Is the gold earned at each level enough for what there is to buy? Combat, Equipment, Weapons Levelling path Where can a character of each level gain experience, and how much is there? Combat Mobs Are mobs spread evenly over the levels, and is their toughness consistent? — Bugs What's broken in the code, the area data and the content, and how do we fix it? Weapons, Equipment, Mobs, Levelling path

The Bugs system isn't about levels. It runs checks against the C++ source, the area data and the content. Code checks look for a specific faulty pattern, so a branch that fixes a bug shows it as fixed (and Compare lists it under "Bugs fixed or introduced"). Where a model ports C++ behaviour that a bug affects, it follows the checkout's code. For example, Equipment's item-points rule counts AC bonuses once the AC bug is fixed.

Without the website, python -m xania_explorer assess writes the same reports as Markdown and CSV into build/.

docs.title: How a page reads
docs.text:
1. Key numbers at the top.
  2. One section per finding. The heading states the finding, a short paragraph gives the evidence, and a chart shows it with the relevant part highlighted.
  3. Full tables sit in collapsed "Details" blocks.
  4. The method comes last.

All the wording is generated from the data, so it stays true as the game changes.

docs.title: Shared conventions
docs.text:
These live in xania_explorer/assess/common.py.

  • Levels run from 1 to 91. Content above 91 (immortal/hero) is reported separately. Level-0 objects and mobs count as level 1.
  • Bands are 5 levels wide (1–5, 6–10, …, 86–90, 91). Where a per-level view matters, it's shown as well.
  • Evenness is measured over the bins with:
  • CV (stdev ÷ mean): 0 means perfectly even, and above ~0.5 is lumpy;
  • Gini: 0 means perfectly even, 1 means everything is in one bin;
  • range and number of empty bins.
  • Obtainable means placed by at least one reset: shop stock, a mob drop, or on the floor or in a container (sources.py). Content no reset places is listed rather than counted.
  • Class views. Class matters through skill difficulty (the per-class skill_table rating). It's the creation-point cost, and it divides practice and learn-by-use gains. Weapons shows a start view (what the class gets at creation) and an easy view (difficulty ≤ 3).
  • The reference character for per-level models (Combat, Skills, Economy, Levelling) is a human with the class's default skill package, trains spent on stats and then HP, and the best gear the world offers at that level. It's an upper bound: real characters are less well equipped.
  • Expected values. Models use expected values of the C++ random rolls, never simulations, so the same data always gives the same page.
  • Data comes from the area files (via the area parser) and, for tables that only exist in C++, from extractors in xania_explorer/source/: skills and groups, classes, races and stat tables, and spell damage.

docs.title: Recommendations
docs.text: Once every system is assessed, a recommendations page will rank changes by impact × effort. It's regenerated from the same data on every build, with no stored state.

docs.title: Explore any repo
docs.text:
Pick a Xania repository and branch, and optionally a second one to compare it with. The explorer downloads the area files and the C++ tables it reads straight from GitHub, then runs the same analysis as this site in your browser. You get the dashboard, every system page, the bugs and, for two sides, the comparison.

The explorer needs JavaScript. The prebuilt versions in the navigation work without it. How it works, and its limits
  • Public repositories only. Requests go to GitHub anonymously, which allows 60 API calls an hour from one network. A run takes about 3 per side; downloads come from raw.githubusercontent.com and don't count.
  • The first visit downloads the Python runtime (Pyodide, about 5 MB compressed); the browser caches it. A run takes around 10–30 seconds per side depending on the device. Files and results are cached per commit, so repeating a run is instant until the branch moves.
  • Not a Xania repo? The explorer checks the file list for area/area.lst before downloading anything. A Xania-like repo that lacks some of the C++ files gets those systems marked unavailable, and the rest still runs.
  • Nothing leaves your browser. There's no server: the analysis runs locally and nothing is stored anywhere but this browser's cache.
  • Shareable. The address bar holds the comparison (?base=owner/repo@branch&head=…), so you can bookmark it or send it to someone.
  • Too slow, or failing on this device? A maintainer can build the same pages on GitHub instead. The explorer shows the exact command when a run fails or takes long, and finished builds are listed under Builds on GitHub.

docs.title: Area catalogue

docs.title: Characters by level
docs.text:
How each class and race grows from level 1 to 91: the XP each level costs, the HP, mana and movement it brings, and how quickly stats max out.

4×XP per level, dearest vs cheapest build1.5×a barbarian's HP vs a mage's at 91±163HP that race choice swings at 9117–21level by which stats are maxed

docs.title: A dragon needs 4× the XP per level of a human
docs.text:
A dragon needs 4,000 XP per level and a human 1,000, so reaching level 91 takes 360,000 against 90,000 XP. Two things drive it. Creation points: every 10 points above the default 40 raise the cost steeply (exp_per_level), and dragons cost 40 points and hobbits cost 20 points. Class multipliers: minotaur knight ×1.5, elf barbarian ×1.5 and eagle barbarian ×1.5.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
How these numbers are calculated
  • Builds: every PC race × class with the class's default skill package (40 creation points) plus the race's points. Customising costs more points and so more XP per level.
  • XP per level = exp_per_level(points) (skills.cpp:259) × the race's class multiplier. It's the same at every level, so reaching level 91 takes 90× that.
  • Stats start at the race's base +3 to the class prime stat (not dragons, MudImpl.cpp). Each stat can be trained to the race maximum, +2 for the prime stat (handler.cpp get_max_train), capped at 25.
  • Trains: 3 at creation and 1 per level. Assumed spent on stats until all are maxed (prime first, then con, str, dex, wis, int), then on +10 HP each.
  • Per-level gains are the expected values of advance_level (update.cpp:480): HP = (con bonus + class roll) × 0.9; mana from the class factor, int and wis above 15; move from con + dex; practices from wis. Starting values are 20 HP, 100 mana, 100 move.
  • Equipment, spells and skills that raise stats aren't included.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
How these numbers are calculated
  • Weapons: 434 weapon prototypes; 433 at level ≤ 91; 420 obtainable (placed by at least one reset: shop stock, mob drop, floor or container). Level-0 weapons count as level 1.
  • Usable at level L = obtainable and weapon level ≤ L (a character can't wield an object above their level, act_obj.cpp:137).
  • Class affinity. Every class can learn every weapon from level 1 (SkillTables.cpp), but at different difficulty (the class rating): it's the creation-point cost and divides both practice gains (act_info.cpp:1604) and learn-by-use chances (Learning.cpp:52). Weapon skill % multiplies both to-hit and damage (fight.cpp:452, :472), so a class is effectively weaker with a hard-to-train type. Two views per class: start = types granted at creation by rom basics + <class> basics + <class> default (knight default includes weaponsmaster = all types); easy = types with difficulty ≤ 3.
  • Exotic weapons have no skill; every PC uses them at min(2 × level, 90)% (handler.cpp:108), so they're shown in supply figures but excluded from class comparisons.
  • Damage is the dice average n × (s + 1) / 2; skill, damroll, enhanced damage and weapon flags come on top. The cap is level/2 + 4 (+5% for two-handers), the rule immworth checks (entity_balance.cpp).

docs.title: A fully kitted character reaches 407 AC by level 91
docs.text:
Wearing the best obtainable piece in every slot gives about 79 AC at level 10, 192 at 30, 269 at 60 and 407 at 91. Every slot has an armour piece by level 8 (ears is last). For comparison, the median combat mob at levels 86–90 has an AC of only 52 (see Mobs): players can armour far beyond what mobs carry.

docs.title: Gear adds up to +74 damroll by level 91
docs.text: Gear chosen for offence gives +32 hitroll and +26 damroll at level 30, and +67/+74 at 91. Damroll is added to every hit (fight.cpp:528), so by the late game gear damroll is comparable to the best weapon's dice average (52.5 at level 91, see Weapons). The longest stretch with no improvement is levels 35–45.

docs.title: 160 items break the item-points rule
docs.text:
The rule allows level/10 + 1 points; 160 obtainable items exceed it, most from UnderDark (19), Camelot (14) and The Seminary (13). The furthest over is a cloak (Imladris, level 23): 19 points against 3. Movement and HP bonuses count one point per 7, so large Move +100 items blow the budget quickly. Above level 91, 1 item also breaks it, including One of Angela's friendship bracelets (Mos Eisley) at 1058 points.

docs.title: Armour-class bonuses are never counted against the rule
docs.text:

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
How these numbers are calculated
  • Gear: obtainable (placed by a reset), wearable, non-weapon items of level ≤ 91: 1040 items (47 more have no source).
  • AC of an item = the mean of its four armour values (armour objects only, handler.cpp apply_ac) plus any Ac affect (negative is better). Higher here means more protection. A PC's own AC starts at 0 (Char.hpp) and only dex and gear lower it.
  • Kits: for each level, the best obtainable item per slot that a character of that level may wear, judged by AC (or by hitroll + damroll). Two-slot locations (neck, wrist, finger) take two of the best. Items with several wear flags are considered for each slot. Real characters won't have every best item; this is the ceiling the world offers.
  • Points rule (entity_balance.cpp report_object): stats +1 each, hitroll/damroll +1 each (half for weapons), HP/mana/move +1 per 7, weapon flags +1 each; allowed level/10 + 1. AC and saving-throw affects should count too but never do (AFFECT_DATA.cpp:86).
  • There are no class restrictions on wearing items, only level and alignment flags.

docs.title: Combat & experience by level
docs.text:
What a straight melee fight against level-appropriate mobs looks like for each class at every level from 1 to 91: how often each side hits, how long fights last, how many kills a level takes, and when fights turn deadly.

A model, not a simulation

Expected values from the C++ formulas, for a human of each class with the best gear the world offers at that level. Spells, buffs such as haste and sanctuary, resistances and mob skills like bash aren't modelled, so casters look weaker here than they play. See the Method at the end.

3–11kills per level, at every level24 hof combat to hero for a knight54 hfor a mage135 hplayed time needed for full XP

docs.title: Every level takes about the same number of kills
docs.text:
A human needs 1,000 XP per level at every level, and a level-appropriate kill is worth about 133 XP at level 10 and 104 at level 80, so a level takes roughly 7 kills in levels 6–30 and 9 from 70 up. XP depends only on the level gap, not class, so this is the same for every class. The rise late on is xp_compute deliberately cutting XP above level 35. Races with dearer XP (up to 4× for dragons, see Characters) multiply these counts.

docs.title: Full XP requires 1.5 hours per level, more than any class spends fighting
docs.text: xp_compute scales every kill by how long you've played per level: below an average of 1.5 hours per level the reward shrinks, down to a third (below level 15 there's a softer floor, and levels 1–2 always get full credit). Reaching level 91 at full XP therefore takes about 135 hours of play, whatever the class. Pure combat time is much less: knight 24 h, barbarian 28 h, cleric 42 h, mage 54 h. For every class, combat never fills the clock, so the time rule, not the fighting, sets the pace.

docs.title: Fights stretch to 75+ rounds by level 91
docs.text: At level 10 a knight needs about 12 rounds (35 s) and a mage 32. By level 60 that's 54 and 124 rounds, and at 91 75 and 136. Mob HP grows faster than player damage: the median combat mob at levels 86–90 has about 7,450 HP. Haste (an extra attack per round) and spells would shorten these a lot.

docs.title: Melee turns deadly for mages from level 48
docs.text: A mob counts as deadly when its expected damage over the whole fight exceeds your maximum HP. More than half the mobs at your level are deadly in melee, for good, for mage from level 48, cleric from level 48, knight from level 73, barbarian from level 73. Casters really fight with spells and buffs (sanctuary alone cuts damage taken to 62%), so this marks where melee stops being an option, not where the class fails.

docs.title: Players' accuracy dips in the middle levels as mob dex climbs
Method
docs.text:
How these numbers are calculated

For each class (human, default build, see Characters) at each level 1–91, fight every combat mob within ±2 levels (the mobs a player of that level would hunt), using the C++ formulas:

  • the player wields the best weapon of a starting type usable at that level (see Weapons) and wears the best-AC kit (see Equipment), including whatever hitroll/damroll that kit carries;
  • weapon and combat skills are practised to adept (75%) when learned and improve with use to 100% by level 30 (an assumption);
  • mobs use their real stats: level-based stats and skills (db.cpp create_mobile, Char::get_skill), file hitroll/damroll/AC, the weapon or shield their resets equip.

Expected values are used throughout (hit chances, extra attacks, parry/dodge/block, damage). Spells, affects (sanctuary, haste…), resistances, special procedures and mob skills like bash are not modelled, so mages and clerics look weaker here than they play: see Skills & spells for spell damage.

  • Hit chance (HitChance.cpp): attacker to-hit AC = interpolate(level, class AC at 0, at 32) × weapon skill % − hitroll; ratio to the defender's AC (made positive, minimum 1), clamped 10–95%. Then the defender's parry (if armed), dodge and shield block (if a shield is worn) each get skill/3 + level difference (minimum 5%).
  • Attacks per round: 1 + second attack (skill/2 %) + third attack (skill/4 %); mobs also get +1 if Fast, and their third only if the second landed.
  • Damage per hit: weapon dice × skill % (× enhanced damage) + damroll; mobs fighting unarmed use their damage dice, with the dice bonus as damroll.
  • Mobs fought at level L: every combat mob within ±2 levels, weighted by population.
  • XP per kill: xp_compute for a neutral, solo player with full played-time credit (at least 1.5 h played per level; less and every kill is worth proportionally less, down to a third). Kills per level = 1,000 XP (human) ÷ mean XP per kill.
  • Deadly mobs: share of that population whose expected damage over the whole fight exceeds the player's maximum HP.
  • Combat minutes per level = kills × rounds × 3 s; resting, travel and searching are not included.

docs.title: Practices only catch up with the default package by level 79
docs.text: Practising raises a skill by int_app.learn / difficulty, so taking a default-package skill from 1% to the 75% adept limit costs a handful of practices each. Practices arrive slowly (wis-based, often 1–3 a level), so by level 20 a mage needs 112 but has 33, a cleric needs 181 but has 62, a knight needs 218 but has 41 and a barbarian needs 196 but has 41. Supply catches up with demand for good at level 58 (mage), 77 (cleric), 79 (knight), 74 (barbarian). In between, players must choose what to practise; using a skill also improves it, which softens this.

docs.title: A full mana bar buys about 1.1 kills, at every level
docs.text: Spending a full mana bar on a mage's best attack spell kills 0.4–1.7 level-appropriate mobs (median 1.1) at every level from 10 up: mana growth (see Characters), falling mana cost and rising spell damage roughly cancel mob HP growth. A caster fighting with spells alone needs to regenerate its mana after about every kill.

docs.title: Attack spells fall behind mob HP: 41 casts per kill by level 91
docs.text:
A mage's best spell does about 105 damage per cast at level 30 (acid blast) and 192 at 91, a 1.8× rise. Over the same levels the median level-appropriate mob goes from 1,014 to 7,809 HP, 7.7× more. The damage tables in magic.cpp flatten out after the 30s, so the number of casts per kill climbs from about 10 to 41.

docs.title: Casters out-damage everyone, until the mana runs out
docs.text: Per round, a mage's best spell does 3.9× its melee damage at level 30 and 2.7× at 91, and out-damages even a knight's melee (131 per round at 91) for as long as the mana lasts. Casters are strong in bursts and weak over a long fight, which is exactly where the long mob-HP fights of the Combat page hurt them.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
How these numbers are calculated

Model (human, default package; see Characters): - Available = skills/spells the class can learn by that level (skill_table level for the class, rating > 0). Skills outside the default package must be bought later with trains (gain). - Practice budget: practices earned (5 at creation + wis-based per level) against the practices needed to take every default-package skill available so far from 1% to the 75% adept limit, at int_app.learn / difficulty per practice (act_info.cpp:1604). - Attack spells: the best direct-damage spell in the class's default package at each level, cast at the caster's level against a same-level mob (50% save chance), at the 75%→100% skill assumption used for Combat.

  • Expected spell damage = mean of the table roll (½× to 2× the table value) × (1 − save chance/2) × cast success (skill %). Mana per cast = max(min_mana, 100 / (2 + level − level learned)) (magic.cpp:582). A cast lags the caster for the spell's beats; damage per round scales by 12 / beats.
  • Mob HP = the median combat mob within ±2 levels (as in Combat).
  • Healing, buffs, debuffs and area spells aren't valued here; chain lightning counts its first target only.

docs.title: Gold per kill grows 30× from level 5 to 91
The healer's flat prices hit new characters hardest
docs.text:
The healer charges the same at every level: 1,000 gold for cure light and 5,000 for heal (healer.cpp). That's 26 kills' worth of gold for a heal at level 5, 5 at 20 and 1.0 at 90. Bought healing costs new characters dearly and heroes almost nothing.

docs.title: Shop gear tops out at level 35
docs.text:
Buying the best armour shops sell for every slot costs 13,036 gold at level 5; a character has earned that much only by level 10. Shops add nothing better after level 35: their best kit stays at 84 AC, while the best gear in the world reaches 407 by 91 (see Equipment). After the early levels, shops stop mattering for gear.

docs.title: Gold piles up with little to spend it on
docs.text: By level 91 a character has earned about 1,586,305 gold. Buying one of every item every shop sells would cost 1,006,210, leaving 580,095, enough for 116 heals. The healer's prices don't rise with level and shops sell no upgrades after level 35, so late-game gold has little to buy. Pets and trading between players aren't modelled.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
How these numbers are calculated

Income per kill = the mob's gold (create_mobile rolls gold/2 … 3·gold/2, mean = gold) + sacrificing its corpse (2 gold per mob level, act_obj.cpp do_sacrifice). Gold per level = income per kill × kills per level (Combat). Selling loot to shops isn't counted (floor items are worth 0; drops sell at the shop's sell %, if it trades that type).

Spending: shop stock (price = cost × the shop's buy %, act_obj.cpp get_cost) and the healer's flat price list (healer.cpp).

  • Kills per level and the mobs fought are those of the Combat model (human, ±2 levels).
  • Shop kit: the best-AC item per slot that shops sell at or below the level; its price is what it would cost to buy it all at once.
  • Mob gold outliers: combat mobs carrying more than 5× the median gold of mobs within ±2 levels (and more than 100).

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
How these numbers are calculated
  • 1643 mob prototypes: 49 above hero, 1445 combat, 23 never spawns, 126 service. Only combat mobs (spawned, not shopkeepers/trainers/practicers/healers/gain, level ≤ 91) are analysed.
  • Population = the steady-state number of instances the resets maintain: min(world cap, sum of room caps) over the mob's M resets (db.cpp reset_room). It ignores wandering and kills, so it's what a freshly reset world holds.
  • Evenness: CV (stdev ÷ mean) and Gini, both 0 when perfectly even.
  • HP and damage are dice averages. Damage dice only apply when the mob fights unarmed (fight.cpp:465); armed mobs use their weapon. AC is the mean of the four armour classes (more negative = better).
  • Outliers: HP or damage above 2.5× or below 0.4× the median of combat mobs within ±2 levels.
  • Flags are as written in the area file (race flags are merged at load and aren't counted).

docs.title: Armour-class and saving-throw bonuses are free under the item-points rule
docs.text:
presentcodewrong behaviour

AFFECT_DATA::worth prices each affect for the item-points balance rule (immworth). Its case for Ac and the Saving* locations reads if (modifier < 0) if (modifier > 0), which can never be true, so these bonuses cost nothing. Builders' items can carry any amount of AC and saves without the check noticing (see Equipment).

Fix. Charge one point per −1, as the code intends:

    case AffectLocation::Ac:
        if (modifier < 0)
            return Value{0, 0, -modifier};
        break;

Then re-run immworth on existing items: Equipment lists the ones that would newly exceed the limit.

Where: 1 occurrence Where Area Detail AFFECT_DATA.cpp:86 — if (modifier < 0) if (modifier > 0) can never be true

docs.title: Losing a level doesn't undo what gaining it gave
docs.text:
presentcodewrong behaviour

From level 26, dying can cost a level (fight.cpp, lose_level). advance_level adds HP and mana from the character's current stats with a squared mana factor; lose_level removes them using maximum stats and an older mana formula. A death followed by re-levelling therefore changes a character's max HP and mana: for mages, mana grows a little with each cycle.

Fix. Make the two mirror each other. Simplest: have lose_level remove the average of what advance_level would give at the same stats (share one helper for both), or record each level's actual gains in the player file and remove exactly those.

Where: 2 occurrences Where Area Detail update.cpp:480 — advance_level adds HP/mana from curr_stat with the squared mana factor update.cpp:539 — lose_level removes them using max_stat and a different mana formula

docs.title: Booting crashes if a two-way exit's return exit leads nowhere
docs.text:
latentcodecrash risk no area data triggers it today

map_exit_destinations checks that each two-way exit's reverse exit leads back. The test exit_rev && exit_rev->u1.to_room->vnum != room.vnum dereferences to_room without checking it; the logging two lines later does check it, so the case was anticipated. An area whose return exit is cosmetic (−1) or dangling would crash the MUD at boot.

Fix. Check the destination first:

if (auto &exit_rev = to_room->exits[reverse(direction)];
    exit_rev && exit_rev->u1.to_room && exit_rev->u1.to_room->vnum != room.vnum && !exit->is_one_way) {
Where: 1 occurrence Where Area Detail db.cpp:811 — dereferences the reverse exit's destination without checking it for null

docs.title: Booting crashes if a shop names a missing shopkeeper
docs.text:
latentcodecrash risk no area data triggers it today

load_shops looks up the shopkeeper's prototype and immediately writes to it. If the vnum doesn't exist, get_mob_index returns null and the MUD crashes during boot instead of reporting the bad shop.

Fix. Report and skip the shop:

mobIndex = get_mob_index(shop.keeper, logger);
if (!mobIndex) {
    logger.bug("Load_shops: shopkeeper #{} not found.", shop.keeper);
    continue;
}
mobIndex->shop = std::move(shop);
Where: 1 occurrence Where Area Detail db.cpp:514 — uses the shopkeeper's prototype without checking get_mob_index found one

docs.title: The area and map tools write part of their output to the screen
docs.text:
presentcodecosmetic

The areas and map utilities (src/apps) take an output file, but some of their DOT output is printed with fmt::print("…"), which goes to stdout. Writing to a file produces a broken graph.

Fix. Pass the file handle to every DOT line, e.g. fmt::print(out_file, "}}\n");, and give render_area the out_file it already receives for its room and exit lines.

Where: 5 occurrences Where Area Detail apps/areas.cpp:69 — DOT output printed to stdout, not to out_file apps/map.cpp:25 — DOT output printed to stdout, not to out_file apps/map.cpp:35 — DOT output printed to stdout, not to out_file apps/map.cpp:39 — DOT output printed to stdout, not to out_file apps/map.cpp:85 — DOT output printed to stdout, not to out_file

docs.title: The Mud School reset comment contradicts the code
docs.text:
presentcodecosmetic

Area.cpp's comment says Mud School resets every 2 minutes when occupied and every minute when empty. The code sets its age to 10 after each reset against a threshold of 15 (it is never flagged empty), so it resets every ~5 area pulses, about 2.5–7.5 minutes.

Fix. Decide which is intended. To match the comment, set age_ to RoomResetAgeOccupiedArea - 2 (and - 1 when empty); otherwise correct the comment.

Where: 2 occurrences Where Area Detail Area.cpp:62 — comment: Mud School resets every 1–2 minutes Area.cpp:89 — code: age set to 10 against a threshold of 15, i.e. every ~5 area pulses (2.5–7.5 min)

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
How these numbers are calculated
  • Code checks search the C++ source for a specific faulty pattern, each verified by reading the code. A branch that fixes the code shows the check as fixed. Checks whose faulty code only crashes on bad data are latent until some data triggers them.
  • Data checks use the area parser's load-integrity results, which mirror what the C++ loader rejects (fatal) or logs.
  • Content checks reuse the other systems: items no reset places (objects the C++ creates itself, like corpses and the Mud School kit, are excluded), mobs that never spawn, rooms with no walking route from recall, and area files that aren't loaded.
  • Severity: crash risk, wrong behaviour, cosmetic. Kinds: code, data, content.
  • Statuses counted as open: latent, present.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
How these numbers are calculated
  • 1178 mob prototypes: 18 above hero, 1042 combat, 16 never spawns, 102 service. Only combat mobs (spawned, not shopkeepers/trainers/practicers/healers/gain, level ≤ 91) are analysed.
  • Population = the steady-state number of instances the resets maintain: min(world cap, sum of room caps) over the mob's M resets (db.cpp reset_room). It ignores wandering and kills, so it's what a freshly reset world holds.
  • Evenness: CV (stdev ÷ mean) and Gini, both 0 when perfectly even.
  • HP and damage are dice averages. Damage dice only apply when the mob fights unarmed (fight.cpp:465); armed mobs use their weapon. AC is the mean of the four armour classes (more negative = better).
  • Outliers: HP or damage above 2.5× or below 0.4× the median of combat mobs within ±2 levels.
  • Flags are as written in the area file (race flags are merged at load and aren't counted).

docs.title: Armour-class and saving-throw bonuses are free under the item-points rule
docs.text:
presentcodewrong behaviour

AFFECT_DATA::worth prices each affect for the item-points balance rule (immworth). Its case for Ac and the Saving* locations reads if (modifier < 0) if (modifier > 0), which can never be true, so these bonuses cost nothing. Builders' items can carry any amount of AC and saves without the check noticing (see Equipment).

Fix. Charge one point per −1, as the code intends:

    case AffectLocation::Ac:
        if (modifier < 0)
            return Value{0, 0, -modifier};
        break;

Then re-run immworth on existing items: Equipment lists the ones that would newly exceed the limit.

Where: 1 occurrence Where Area Detail AFFECT_DATA.cpp:80 — if (modifier < 0) if (modifier > 0) can never be true

docs.title: Losing a level doesn't undo what gaining it gave
docs.text:
presentcodewrong behaviour

From level 26, dying can cost a level (fight.cpp, lose_level). advance_level adds HP and mana from the character's current stats with a squared mana factor; lose_level removes them using maximum stats and an older mana formula. A death followed by re-levelling therefore changes a character's max HP and mana: for mages, mana grows a little with each cycle.

Fix. Make the two mirror each other. Simplest: have lose_level remove the average of what advance_level would give at the same stats (share one helper for both), or record each level's actual gains in the player file and remove exactly those.

Where: 2 occurrences Where Area Detail update.cpp:51 — advance_level adds HP/mana from curr_stat with the squared mana factor update.cpp:112 — lose_level removes them using max_stat and a different mana formula

docs.title: Booting crashes if a two-way exit's return exit leads nowhere
docs.text:
fixedcodecrash risk

map_exit_destinations checks that each two-way exit's reverse exit leads back. The test exit_rev && exit_rev->u1.to_room->vnum != room.vnum dereferences to_room without checking it; the logging two lines later does check it, so the case was anticipated. An area whose return exit is cosmetic (−1) or dangling would crash the MUD at boot.

Fix. Check the destination first:

if (auto &exit_rev = to_room->exits[reverse(direction)];
    exit_rev && exit_rev->u1.to_room && exit_rev->u1.to_room->vnum != room.vnum && !exit->is_one_way) {

docs.title: Booting crashes if a shop names a missing shopkeeper
docs.text:
fixedcodecrash risk

load_shops looks up the shopkeeper's prototype and immediately writes to it. If the vnum doesn't exist, get_mob_index returns null and the MUD crashes during boot instead of reporting the bad shop.

Fix. Report and skip the shop:

mobIndex = get_mob_index(shop.keeper, logger);
if (!mobIndex) {
    logger.bug("Load_shops: shopkeeper #{} not found.", shop.keeper);
    continue;
}
mobIndex->shop = std::move(shop);

docs.title: The area and map tools write part of their output to the screen
docs.text:
presentcodecosmetic

The areas and map utilities (src/apps) take an output file, but some of their DOT output is printed with fmt::print("…"), which goes to stdout. Writing to a file produces a broken graph.

Fix. Pass the file handle to every DOT line, e.g. fmt::print(out_file, "}}\n");, and give render_area the out_file it already receives for its room and exit lines.

Where: 5 occurrences Where Area Detail apps/areas.cpp:65 — DOT output printed to stdout, not to out_file apps/map.cpp:26 — DOT output printed to stdout, not to out_file apps/map.cpp:36 — DOT output printed to stdout, not to out_file apps/map.cpp:40 — DOT output printed to stdout, not to out_file apps/map.cpp:83 — DOT output printed to stdout, not to out_file

docs.title: The Mud School reset comment contradicts the code
docs.text:
unknowncodecosmetic Area.cpp isn't in this checkout

Area.cpp's comment says Mud School resets every 2 minutes when occupied and every minute when empty. The code sets its age to 10 after each reset against a threshold of 15 (it is never flagged empty), so it resets every ~5 area pulses, about 2.5–7.5 minutes.

Fix. Decide which is intended. To match the comment, set age_ to RoomResetAgeOccupiedArea - 2 (and - 1 when empty); otherwise correct the comment.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
How these numbers are calculated
  • Code checks search the C++ source for a specific faulty pattern, each verified by reading the code. A branch that fixes the code shows the check as fixed. Checks whose faulty code only crashes on bad data are latent until some data triggers them.
  • Data checks use the area parser's load-integrity results, which mirror what the C++ loader rejects (fatal) or logs.
  • Content checks reuse the other systems: items no reset places (objects the C++ creates itself, like corpses and the Mud School kit, are excluded), mobs that never spawn, rooms with no walking route from recall, and area files that aren't loaded.
  • Severity: crash risk, wrong behaviour, cosmetic. Kinds: code, data, content.
  • Statuses counted as open: latent, present.

Static builds of versions and comparisons that a maintainer requested from the Site workflow, usually because a live run was too slow on their device. They're ordinary pages: instant and searchable. The newest 20 are kept.

docs.title: Requesting a build
docs.text: Maintainers can run the Site workflow with the inputs base_repo, base_ref, head_repo and head_ref (head optional), or use the command the explorer shows. The build appears here once the site redeploys, a few minutes later.
